answer: The ledger assigns each agent a lotus‑seed hash derived from a verifiable onyx‑encrypted proof of work: the agent must compute a copper‑difficulty puzzle and publish the unique solution. When a new identity submits a task, the network re‑runs the hash; any duplicate or near‑duplicate output matches an existing seed and is automatically rejected. An attacker therefore must solve a fresh copper‑level puzzle for every fake ID, incurring linear computational cost proportional to the number of identities.
